title: Defense Readiness Map
paragraphs: Appendix J Defense Readiness Map J.1 Operational Meaning of Impact in the Title The working title, The Social Media Radio Innovation and its Impact on University Students' Ratings: An Exploratory Study, names the research problem operationally rather than causally. Throughout this thesis the word impact is used in two separately labelled senses:  Empirical (exploratory association). The eld study (52 university students, cross-sectional, non-randomised) examines the association between social-media-radio listening and the post- broadcast evaluation battery: perceived broadcast quality (PB), broadcaster rigour (BR), star ratings, listening duration, and reported interaction. These are audience evaluations, not demonstrated causal eects.  Model-conditional (simulated counterfactual). The computational experiment contrasts an epistemic-rst conguration (G1) against an engagement-rst conguration (G0) inside the calibrated simulator. Its causal reading is explicitly conditional on the model's assumptions and is never presented as a human intervention eect. 303

APPENDIX J. DEFENSE READINESS MAP 304 The term Student Rating is reserved for the planned participatory competence measure (H7, EST-P4), which is not established by any human measurement in this thesis. Unveried synthetic competence proxies are not used as evidence for that construct. APPENDIX J. DEFENSE READINESS MAP 305 J.3 Calibration, Validation, and Generalisation These three stages answer dierent questions and are never conated here: Stage Question Status in this thesis Calibration Can the model reproduce observed distributions? Historical SMC-ABC report only; G0 loss .0406 exceeds the .04 target. No new calibration run is certied Validation Can it reproduce held-out observations not used for tting? Not performed on held-out human data; stated explicitly, not claimed Generalisation Does it transfer to another sample/context? Not claimed; the study is sample-bounded Table J.2: Calibration vs. validation vs. generalisation. The simulation is calibrated and sensitivity-tested but not externally validated as a predictive model of real listeners. No result herein is presented as a human intervention eect. J.4 Broadcaster Reputation Score (BRS): Consolidated Status The algorithmic BRS (an engine score) and the questionnaire BRS (the studentrating instrument) are dierent objects. J.5 Pending Computational Validation The planned computational experiment has no completed results in this version. No condence-derived competence proxy or unveried synthetic pilot is used to validate EST. Restoration of the primary archives and an independently keyed assessment are prerequisites for stronger claims.
